content.user_title: Learn to Create Claude Code Skills
content.value_statement: Authoring a Claude Code Skill is confusing without a clear reference for file structure and metadata rules. This guide explains the required layout, naming, and progressive disclosure patterns so you can build a working Skill correctly.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md file and its YAML frontmatter fields.
Shows the recommended directory layout for a Claude Code Skill.
Describes the progressive disclosure pattern using supporting files.
Lists technical limits for name and description field lengths.
Provides naming guidance with recommended and discouraged examples.
Demonstrates how to organize multiple related Skills by function.
limitations: This is a reference guide, not an automated tool that generates Skills.
The main content is written in Chinese, which may not suit every reader.
It does not validate an existing Skill or check it for errors.
It covers structure and naming, not advanced scripting inside Skills.

use_cases.title: Author a first Claude Code Skill
use_cases.description: A developer new to Claude Code follows the file structure and metadata rules to build a valid Skill from scratch.

use_cases.title: Organize a library of related Skills
use_cases.description: A team lead uses the function-based directory layout to group many Skills so they stay easy to maintain and reference.

use_cases.title: Apply progressive disclosure to large Skills
use_cases.description: A technical writer splits a complex Skill into supporting files so Claude reads only what it needs and context stays efficient.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the basic structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the minimum files and metadata a Claude Code Skill needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a named Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a SKILL.md for a Skill that processes PDF files, following the recommended naming rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add supporting files
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to split my large Skill into supporting files using the progressive disclosure pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a multi-Skill project
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a directory layout for a project that contains PDF processing, Excel analysis, and code review Skills.

output_examples.input: Explain the minimum files and metadata a Claude Code Skill needs.
output_examples.output: A Claude Code Skill requires a SKILL.md file. That file must include YAML frontmatter with a name and a description. The name may be up to 64 characters and the description up to 1024 characters. The body of the file gives step-by-step instructions and examples for Claude to follow.

output_examples.input: Show me how to organize a project with several related Skills.
output_examples.output: Group related Skills under a .claude/skills directory. Give each Skill its own subfolder, such as pdf-processing, excel-analysis, or code-review. Each subfolder holds its own SKILL.md. This layout keeps Skills easy to reference and maintain.

best_practices: Keep the main SKILL.md body under 500 lines for best performance.
Use clear action-based names like Processing PDFs instead of vague labels.
Move optional detail into supporting files and load them only when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague names such as Helper, Utils, or Tools.
Do not nest file references deeply beyond one level.
Do not place every detail in one large file instead of supporting files.

faq.question: What file does every Claude Code Skill require?
faq.answer: Every Skill requires a SKILL.md file. This file holds the YAML frontmatter and the instructions Claude follows.

faq.question: What are the metadata length limits?
faq.answer: The name field may be up to 64 characters. The description field may be up to 1024 characters.

faq.question: What is progressive disclosure?
faq.answer: Progressive disclosure means Claude reads supporting files only when they are needed. This keeps the context efficient for large Skills.

faq.question: Where can I store my Skills?
faq.answer: You can store personal Skills under your home directory at ~/.claude/skills. You can store project Skills under .claude/skills in the project.

faq.question: How should I name a Skill?
faq.answer: Use a clear action-based name such as Processing PDFs. Avoid vague or generic names like Helper or Data.

faq.question: Is this skill a tool or a guide?
faq.answer: This skill is a reference guide. It explains how to author a Skill but does not generate one for you.
